issues.legal_issue: A court exercising jurisdiction under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 cannot modify an arbitral award and may interfere only on the statutory grounds for setting it aside.

A court exercising appellate jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 cannot reappraise the merits of an arbitral award or exceed the limits of interference applicable under Section 34.

An arbitral award may not be set aside on public-policy grounds merely because a court disagrees with the arbitrator’s plausible assessment of the evidence or conclusions on contractual delay and compensation.
The contractor was entitled to interest on the arbitral award, and the Court could set the applicable post-award, pendente lite, and future interest rate in exercise of its powers under Article 142.
